question: How's the US yield curve looking — is the 2s10s still inverted, and where are short-term money-market rates sitting?

raw_responses.futures_positioning_summary: 2Y COT crowded (score 56, positioned for lower yields, HFs trimming); 10Y leaning (score 80, asset managers for lower yields, HFs adding); 30Y leaning (score 69).
raw_responses.rate_positioning_summary: TLT (20y+) positioning_score -0.4428 and IEF (7-10y) -0.1071 → options market leaning slightly toward HIGHER long-end yields (bond prices down).
raw_responses.news_summary: Several hawkish Fed items: 4 regional Fed banks backed a discount-rate hike in July minutes; Boston Fed's Collins and Chair Warsh signalled tightening/strict 2% target; UBS still expects a hold at 3.50-3.75%. Falling crude helped push yields lower intraday.
raw_responses._note: Full news[] array and full rate_positioning options detail returned by the server were verbose; the load-bearing curve/slope/macro_drivers are captured verbatim above.

answer_to_user: The US curve is NO LONGER inverted — it's normalized and positively sloped. 2s10s sits at +45.9bp (2Y 4.25% vs 10Y 4.71%), so the classic inversion has un-inverted; the 10Y–3M spread is also positive at +91.4bp, near 52-week highs. The full curve: 3M 3.79%, 2Y 4.25%, 5Y 4.42%, 10Y 4.71%, 30Y 5.24%. On the short/money-market end, the 3-month bill yields 3.79% and the fed funds effective rate is 3.63% (Fed's target range held at 3.50-3.75% in July), so cash still yields well under the belly and long end. Recent moves: the long end has been steepening (30Y +15bp on the month, 10Y +10bp) while short rates drifted lower (3M -6bp/mo). Drivers are sticky inflation (CPI 3.3%, core PCE 3.3%, both rising) plus a soft July payrolls print (-23k) — and Fed commentary has skewed hawkish (four regional banks backed a discount-rate hike; Warsh reaffirming a hard 2% target), consistent with options/COT positioning leaning toward higher long-end yields.
